memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But only you and your sons may serve as priests in connection with everything at the altar and inside the curtain. I am giving you the service of the priesthood as a gift. Anyone else who comes near the sanctuary is to be put to death." — Num 18:7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God calls the priesthood a gift: "I am giving you the service of the priesthood as a gift." What a way to describe the demanding, weighty work of serving at the altar. To Aaron, being allowed to draw near to God and minister in His presence was not a chore to endure but a privilege to treasure.

This turns our usual thinking upside down. We often view service as a cost, something that drains us and demands sacrifice. But God invites us to see it as a gift — the gift of being allowed to come near Him and be used by Him. The privilege of serving a holy God is greater than any comfort we might give up for it.

Consider what a gift it truly is. Sinful people, who by rights could not even approach God and live, are invited to serve in His very presence. That access, that nearness, that usefulness in His work, is pure grace. The priest did not earn his place; God gave it to him. And so it is with every calling to serve God.

Under the new covenant, this gift is opened wide. Peter tells us that all who belong to Christ are now "a royal priesthood." Through Jesus, our great High Priest, every believer is given the astonishing privilege of drawing near to God and serving Him. We do not approach on our own merit — "anyone else who comes near" could not — but through Christ, the way stands open. The next time serving God feels like a burden, remember: it is a gift, the gift of nearness to the God who made you and loves you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you view serving God as a burden or as a gift?
2. What privilege of nearness to God might you be taking for granted?
3. How does being part of a "royal priesthood" in Christ change your service?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me when I treat serving You as a burden rather than the gift it is. Thank You for the privilege of drawing near to You through Christ. Help me to treasure the grace of being useful in Your work. Amen.
